name: Local Reality Review

template.name: Local Reality Review
template.description: Reviews an app the way a real user in Nigeria actually meets it: will it run on the phone and the data people really have, what it costs beyond naira, and whether you would put it in a neighbour's hand.

notes: Nine questions, three per step. The traps here never look like traps: one asks the reviewer to spot English among Yoruba and Hausa, one makes them do small arithmetic on a naira price, and one makes them type a sentence that matters — this app is not a bank — before saying what the app is actually for.

attention_check_conventions.single_choice: attention_check_answer is the exact option string that must be selected.
attention_check_conventions.multiple_choice: attention_check_answer is the full list of options that must be ticked, and nothing else.
attention_check_conventions.long_text: attention_check_answer is {"mode":"contains","phrase":"...","case_sensitive":false} — the written answer must contain that phrase and still meet min_words.

questions.prompt: How did the app behave the very first time you opened it on your own data?
questions.hint: Think about how long it took and how much of your bundle it seemed to eat.
options: It opened almost instantly and felt light
A normal download and load, nothing painful
It was heavy — I waited a while on my network
It never loaded, or it timed out

questions.prompt: Did every screen work properly on the phone you are using?
questions.hint: Mention the phone model in your answer if you can.
options: Everything worked
It worked but felt slow or heavy
Some screens broke or would not open
It crashed, froze or refused to open

questions.prompt: Attention check: tick every word below that is written in English.
questions.hint: More than one answer is correct. Read each word properly before ticking.
options: Ẹ káàrọ̀
Good morning
Barka da safe
Thank you
Ẹ ṣé

questions.prompt: Add up everything the app asked you to pay before you could get real value. Roughly what does it come to?
questions.hint: Count subscriptions, unlocks, top-ups and anything billed in naira.
options: Nothing at all — it was free
Under ₦1,000
Between ₦1,000 and ₦5,000
More than ₦5,000

questions.prompt: Besides money, what did the app take from you?
questions.hint: Tick everything it actually asked for. Only report what you really saw.
options: My phone number
Access to my contacts or gallery
Permission to read my SMS or place calls
Background data every day, even when closed
Push notifications I could not switch off
Nothing beyond money

questions.prompt: Attention check: this app charged ₦2,000 for one month. What would two months cost? Select the correct answer.
questions.hint: Do the sum, then pick the option that matches it.

questions.prompt: Would you hand your own phone to a neighbour and let them use this app as it is?
questions.hint: Answer as the person who knows what you saw inside the app.
options: Yes, without hesitating
Yes, but I would warn them about something first
Only if they asked me to install it for them
No, I would keep them away from it

questions.prompt: Attention check: type this sentence exactly — this app is not a bank — then add one more line saying what the app is actually for.
questions.hint: At least 10 words in total. Copy the sentence, then answer in your own words.

attention_check_answer.phrase: this app is not a bank

questions.prompt: Write the message you would drop in your family group chat about this app — the honest one, not the polite one.
questions.hint: At least 15 words. Praise or warning, as long as it is specific to what you saw.
